concept.name: Triple exponential moving average
concept.definition: Patrick Mulloy's Triple Exponential Moving Average, which extends DEMA with a third smoothing layer, combining single, double, and triple EMAs to remove even more lag for short-term trading.
concept.intuition: DEMA with one more correction term — closer still to price, noisier still.
concept.mechanics: TEMA = 3*EMA1 - 3*EMA2 + EMA3, where EMA2 = EMA(EMA1) and EMA3 = EMA(EMA2). Used via price crosses or fast/slow TEMA crossovers, which fire earlier than equivalent DEMA or EMA crosses; default 20 periods.
concept.failure_modes: Minimal lag means minimal noise filtering — it whipsaws the most of the EMA family in sideways markets, and some lag is actually useful for longer-term analysis.
concept.misconceptions: Faster is not universally better: TEMA's responsiveness amplifies noise, so it is not a straight upgrade over EMA or DEMA. Also, TEMA is not TRIX — TRIX is the 1-period rate of change of a triple EMA.

citations.source: Triple Exponential Moving Average (TEMA) | ChartSchool | StockCharts.com
